PullRequest.Title: agentHost: link cross-chat requests to their sending turns
PullRequest.Body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.

Refs microsoft/vscode-internalbacklog#10773.

A peer chat's reply can start a new turn long after the request that asked for it. `agentHost.userMessageSent` and `agentHost.turnCompleted` now carry `originatingTriggerId` when the host can identify that request. The kickoff, peer work and return reply can be grouped directly under one root; a later independent human request starts its own group. The root is scoped by `originatingTriggerSessionId` and `originatingTriggerChatSessionId`; `originatingTriggerKind` distinguishes a user request from an automation occurrence.

For the immediate sender, `agentHost.userMessageSent` also carries the optional `(sourceAgentSessionId, sourceChatSessionId, sourceTurnId)`. This is useful for inspecting individual hops; the root grouping doesn't require walking those hops in the query. `send_message` may also provide `delegationMessageId` and `delegationMessageRevision` for the admitted version. The chat ID uses the same hashing as the destination field. Only UUID-shaped session/message IDs and UUID or `request_<UUID>` turn IDs are eligible.

The host matches the provider callback to its observed tool start. This identifies the worker chat and execution turn even when a different turn is active in the parent chat. Codex retains the invocation's call ID across approval. Source evidence stays with the individual in-memory message version; expired, ambiguous, client-supplied or restored evidence leaves the source tuple absent. Queue replacement permissions continue to use their existing ownership check. For GitHub standard rows the sender's session column is `conversationId`.

This enriches existing events without adding admissions or changing token/credit counters. A new worker can inherit the root from its exact spawning call. A confirmed steering chain uses the known trigger of its original turn; a fresh idle/queued delivery uses its admitted input. Reused workers without assignment-specific evidence and unrecoverable origins remain unattributed.

**Manual verification (Windows Code OSS):** Started a human request in A that created peer B. B queued a reply while A was handling a *different* human turn. The reply displayed and was acknowledged after that turn finished. Then a user asked an independent question directly in B. The local telemetry log contained five distinct admissions:

| Admission | Recorded source |
|---|---|
| A: original human request | — |
| B: peer kickoff | A's original human turn |
| A: intervening human turn | — |
| A: queued reply from B | B's kickoff turn, message ID and revision 1 |
| B: independent human follow-up | — |

Following those edges grouped 12 distinct matched `copilotSdk/response.success` calls as **9** for the original request (including the peer kickoff and reply), **2** for the intervening request, and **1** for the independent follow-up.

**Worker overlap, corrected build:** A request spawned a background worker; a different parent request was active when the worker sent `WORKER_LATE` to the peer. The receiving admission's source chat and turn matched the worker's successful `agentHost.toolInvoked(send_message)` row. The worker's `turnCompleted.parentTurnId` matched the request that spawned it. The unrelated parent successor completed after the send and was absent from the source tuple. These were local Copilot OSS runs; the delayed Codex approval case was verified in a deterministic test. Production ingestion has not been verified.

**Direct-root verification (Nov 20, Windows Code OSS):** Verified both the admission and completion rows of five turns. The queued reply `074d5ca1…` reported `sourceTurnId=bda55b46…` (the peer) and `originatingTriggerId=request_6f4c48ad…` (the original human request). The root session and chat matched the original admission. The intervening human request and the peer's later human follow-up each reported their own root, so grouping the five completion rows by trigger gives three executions for the original request and one for each independent request.

Scenarios.Scenario: Admit and complete direct human or automation turns, including later independent requests.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Admission runs the new UUID validation, chat-ID hashing and trigger-object construction synchronously before the existing provider send path. Attachments, outgoing contributions, provider preparation and any required checkpoint still precede agent.chats.sendMessage. Telemetry network delivery is not awaited.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Serialize existing telemetry events with additional ID/kind fields.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Same existing admission/completion events; a fixed number of additional scalar properties, not one record per ancestor or peer.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same events were already constructed and serialized, without root dimensions.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Small event construction/serialization is synchronous; network completion is off the turn critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: POST the existing GitHub admission telemetry envelope.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing POST per emitted GitHub admission event; no new event, retry or ancestor fan-out.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Fire-and-forget fetch, not awaited by admission.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Dispatch admitted prompt through the provider's existing SDK/app-server path, which performs model requests.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One unchanged provider send per dispatched turn; internal model/tool iterations are not multiplied by attribution.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same admission-to-provider call path and ordering.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Provider dispatch and subsequent model work determine response progress.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One small trigger object per eligible admitted user/automation turn; four additional root dimensions per existing admission/completion row. Work does not traverse prompt text or transcript history.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Existing per-chat active-turn semantics remain. Independent chats may execute concurrently. Trigger computation is synchronous bounded work; telemetry POSTs remain fire-and-forget.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Trigger construction is once per admission. Existing active-turn state is released on completion; historical root timings retain the small trigger until existing truncation/session cleanup. No new cache keys, history copies or provider discovery are introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the diff only adds fixed-size trigger construction and dimensions to existing telemetry, and the provider-send path is unchanged.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: No measured serialization or allocation timings. Long-session prevalence is unknown, but added state is small and follows existing owners.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: no extra expensive calls, full-content transformations, hot history scans or lost cleanup ownership.

Scenarios.Scenario: Create an independent delegated session or a peer chat and send its initial prompt.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: One source lookup precedes existing argument/catalog/model resolution, optional workspace preparation, session/chat creation, rename and initial-message admission. Creation/preparation must finish before the delegated work can start.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read the registered session catalog and, only for ineligible rows, prefetch session state and resolve provider metadata.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Zero catalog requests for create_session without a workspace; one request when required, or one for legacy create_chat. Concurrent requests share computations. Each computation bulk-reads central rows; fallback costs scale with F ineligible sessions, with prewarming grouped by provider.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical conditional catalog calls, grouping, coalescing and fallback cardinality.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required catalog resolution is awaited before creation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve credential-scoped model choices when needed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one lazy catalog promise per creation invocation; local getModels is used without credential-scoped discovery when appropriate.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same lazy model reader and call count.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited only where model resolution requires it.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Prepare optional folder/worktree or scratch storage and persist session/chat registration and title.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing preparation/creation sequence per requested new destination, with optional worktree operations based on arguments.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same preparation, creation, cleanup and rename sequence.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required destination initialization is awaited before kickoff.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Start the delegated prompt on the existing provider route.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One initial turn per successful creation, as before.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: startPrompt constructed the same Message before calling _startSessionMessage; startMessage now receives that message already constructed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Destination work starts after admission; provider backing may materialize on first send as before.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: K creation invocations and T currently in-flight tool calls. New source resolution scans T live timings once per invocation; it does not scan completed tool history. Existing defaults allow 50 session creations and 50 chat creations per source session per hour, not a global concurrency bound.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: No new global limiter or scheduling. Fresh independent creations can overlap; named session creations use the existing per-session sequencer. Catalog fallback processing uses Limiter(4), and provider prewarming is grouped once per fallback provider.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: create_session only reads the session catalog when its workspace argument requires it. Its model reader is lazy and memoizes one promise per invocation. Concurrent listings coalesce by mode/registry epoch; eligible central catalog rows avoid provider/session-db fallback. Attribution uses a WeakMap keyed by the exact message, so restored/copied messages have no evidence and do not trigger recovery reads.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: before/after call sequences and lazy catalog/model behavior are explicit. The new source scan operates only on live timings, whose completion and turn teardown remove entries.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Aggregate in-flight tool count across independent sessions is not measured. No substantial latency mechanism was established from the simple live-entry comparisons at realistic counts.
Scenarios.Verdict: No high-confidence actionable performance regression. Existing expensive creation/catalog work is neither multiplied nor moved, and source attribution does not recover lineage through external reads.

Scenarios.Scenario: Send a peer reply to an idle or busy chat, then replace or cancel a queued version.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Source lookup and the existing listSessions request precede target validation. Normal sends enter the per-target sequencer, restore a cold destination if necessary, then queue or admit one Message. Replacement/cancellation updates existing pending state without starting additional provider work.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve the existing destination session catalog.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One listSessions request per send/replace/cancel operation, with overlapping requests coalesced and central rows bulk-read; fallback work is per ineligible session, not newly per source attribution.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Every operation already called listSessions at the same position.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited before target validation and queueing.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Restore destination session storage and lazily hydrate its provider backing/history.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One shared restore per cold session and shared hydration per cold chat; no restore when getChatState already exists. Failed attempts may retry on later sends as before.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same cold-state guard, restore/hydration ownership and sequencer ordering.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Cold restore completes inside the per-target send sequencer before queue-versus-start selection.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Publish pending-message state or admit one provider turn when the destination is idle.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One pending-state action or one admission per ordinary send; replacement creates one replacement action, and cancellation one removal action. Later queue draining produces the existing admission, not an extra attribution-only turn.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same queue/start decision and state-action/provider-send counts; only message construction and private attribution placement changed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Busy replies await ordinary queue drain; idle replies use the existing turn send path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: K message operations, T live tool calls, C distinct target chats and F catalog fallback sessions. New attribution stores one small source/version record per exact live Message. Ordinary sends retain the existing 100-per-source-session/hour limit; replacement/cancellation do not obtain a new global limit.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Normal sends are serialized per target chat by SequencerByKey; different targets can proceed concurrently. Catalog work occurs before that sequencer and retains existing coalescing/fallback limiting. Replacement/cancellation remains synchronous after catalog resolution.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: listSessions coalesces concurrent mode/epoch computations, but settled results are removed rather than permanently cached. Cold target restoration is shared per session and hydration per chat; warm target state bypasses restore. Failed restores clear in-flight state for retry. WeakMap attribution neither retains dead message versions nor reconstructs restored evidence.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: per-target serialization, cold/warm guards, restore coalescing and replacement ownership were inspected. No new database, provider or transcript read was added for attribution.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Catalog size, reply rates and restore duration vary and were not measured. They affect unchanged costs, not diff-introduced boundary fan-out.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression. Added live-source lookup and WeakMap/version bookkeeping do not change expensive-boundary cardinality or queue scheduling.

Scenarios.Scenario: Track provider-promoted steering successors and background workers after the parent turn finishes.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Provider progress already arrives before host tracking. The diff finds the pending steering message using the same collection search as the former some(), and obtains worker roots from a direct live spawning-call lookup. Every tool start on a steering successor may read the provider's interaction snapshot synchronously; completion performs the already-existing interaction read.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Consume existing provider turn/tool/worker progress and publish existing state actions.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Same progress and state actions per promoted turn or worker event; no new provider request or worker assignment.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same event handling and turn creation; steering detection used some() instead of find().
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Host tracking remains on the progress callback path but does not wait on additional external operations.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Report completion with a fixed root tuple.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing completion report per execution; no per-ancestor or per-interaction additional event.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Completion already collected provider turn interaction and emitted the report without root dimensions.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing completion reporting path; root lookup is in memory.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Tool starts in steering successor turns, pending steering-message count, and live/historical root timing entries. Copilot's interaction snapshots copy at most 64 IDs from an LRU with 1000 turns, not full transcript/model history.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous host progress processing remains unchanged. Attribution introduces no asynchronous task, fan-out, ancestor traversal or new worker spawn; independent workers retain their existing provider concurrency.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Non-steering trigger access is a direct map lookup. Copilot getTurnInteraction uses live chat maps plus the bounded interaction LRU. Roots are shared small ID objects; tool timings clear on completion/turn teardown, root timings on existing truncation/session disposal. Reused workers without fresh evidence perform no external recovery lookup.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the only implemented getTurnInteraction resolves bounded in-memory snapshots, and its interaction array cap was verified. Spawn lookup is direct and lifecycle cleanup is preserved.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Steering/tool-start frequency is not profiled. The extra snapshot allocation is bounded to 64 references and does not establish substantial CPU/GC pressure on realistic usage.
Scenarios.Verdict: No high-confidence regression. Repeated snapshot reads are new on steering tool starts, but bounded cheap local work is insufficient evidence for a performance finding; no heavyweight synchronous provider read exists.

Scenarios.Scenario: Execute a Codex delegation callback after delayed approval while a successor turn changes the item map.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The existing app-server callback resolves its pending item, possibly awaits approval, executes the same host tool once and returns its result. The diff captures the delegation call ID before approval instead of rereading it afterward.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Receive an existing app-server dynamic-tool RPC, publish an approval request when required, and return the host-tool result.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One callback and response per invocation; one existing approval flow when required; one unchanged host.executeTool call after acceptance.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same RPC/approval/execution count; delegation calls reread the item map after approval.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Approval and tool execution are awaited exactly as before.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One pending callback per dynamic tool invocation, regardless of approval duration or number of later turns. Captured state is an ID/reference, not an approval-time transcript snapshot.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Pending approvals await their own decisions; other turns may progress meanwhile as before. Host delegation tools retain the creation/send concurrency and per-target ordering described above.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Uses existing thread/session and item-to-tool maps. Capturing the call ID does not introduce caches, retry loops, successor-turn scans or restored attribution recovery.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: changed code only pins and selects the call ID; approval and executeTool await structure is unchanged.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Approval wait durations and overlapping-turn frequency are unknown but are not increased by this change.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance regression or concrete performance-regression fix: this is attribution/correlation behavior, with unchanged expensive execution and IPC cardinality.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance-review pass over all 17 changed files and every diff page against base 0ef13631279578789d51cdac61c7e58acb3d2d2e. Investigated new global live-tool scans, steering snapshot reads, weak attribution ownership, historical root retention, telemetry serialization, delegated creation/delivery, cold restoration, catalog grouping/coalescing and delayed Codex approval. No high-confidence diff-introduced performance findings and no qualifying performance-regression fix. Static review only; no runtime performance measurements.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
